records.source: Measure hands this hook a float32 copy of the channels (it reads :attr:`measures_in_float`), so the division happens in float and the measured image is the float result: nothing is rounded and nothing is clipped at the top of the acquisition dtype. Float input is returned in its own float dtype with no rounding and no clipping at all.
records.translation: Measure entrega a este hook una copia float32 de los canales (lee :attr:`measures_in_float`), de modo que la división se hace en coma flotante y la imagen medida es el resultado flotante: no se redondea nada ni se recorta nada en el máximo del dtype de adquisición. Una entrada flotante se devuelve en su propio dtype flotante, sin ningún redondeo ni recorte.

records.context: Integer input -- a direct caller, or a segmentation input that has to keep its dtype -- is corrected in float32 and cast back by *rounding to nearest*:
records.label: spacr.illumination.IlluminationCorrector#3
records.source: Integer input -- a direct caller, or a segmentation input that has to keep its dtype -- is corrected in float32 and cast back by *rounding to nearest*:
records.translation: Una entrada entera -- una llamada directa, o una entrada de segmentación que debe conservar su dtype -- se corrige en float32 y se vuelve a convertir *redondeando al más cercano*:

records.context: **round, not truncate.** Truncation would shave a mean of 0.5 counts off every corrected pixel. Averaged over a 500-pixel object that does not wash out -- it is a systematic, one-directional shift of exactly the kind this feature exists to remove. Rounding is unbiased.
records.label: spacr.illumination.IlluminationCorrector#4
records.source: **round, not truncate.** Truncation would shave a mean of 0.5 counts off every corrected pixel. Averaged over a 500-pixel object that does not wash out -- it is a systematic, one-directional shift of exactly the kind this feature exists to remove. Rounding is unbiased.
records.translation: **redondear, no truncar.** Truncar restaría una media de 0.5 cuentas a cada píxel corregido. Promediado sobre un objeto de 500 píxeles, eso no se diluye -- es un desplazamiento sistemático y en un solo sentido, exactamente del tipo que esta función existe para eliminar. El redondeo no tiene sesgo.

records.context: **rescale, not clip, at the top.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the microscope field of view can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Clipping would remove real signal from exactly the brightest objects, so the whole microscope field of view is instead multiplied by ``dtype max / field max``. That factor is printed and kept per microscope field of view in ``.stats['scales']``.
records.label: spacr.illumination.IlluminationCorrector#5
records.source: **rescale, not clip, at the top.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the field can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Clipping would remove real signal from exactly the brightest objects, so the whole field is instead multiplied by ``dtype max / field max``. That factor is printed and kept per field in ``.stats['scales']``.
records.translation: **reescalar, no recortar, en el máximo.** Una ganancia superior a 1 en el borde del campo puede llevar un píxel casi a fondo de escala más allá del máximo de un uint16. Recortar eliminaría señal real precisamente de los objetos más brillantes, así que en su lugar todo el campo se multiplica por ``dtype max / field max``. Ese factor se imprime y se guarda por campo en ``.stats['scales']``.

records.context: **clip, and count, at the bottom.** A dark offset larger than a pixel gives a negative value, which an unsigned dtype cannot hold; those pixels are clipped to zero, counted and reported.
records.label: spacr.illumination.IlluminationCorrector#6
records.source: **clip, and count, at the bottom.** A dark offset larger than a pixel gives a negative value, which an unsigned dtype cannot hold; those pixels are clipped to zero, counted and reported.
records.translation: **recortar, y contar, en el mínimo.** Un desplazamiento de oscuridad mayor que el valor de un píxel da un valor negativo, que un dtype sin signo no puede almacenar; esos píxeles se recortan a cero, se cuentan y se notifican.
